problem: 'even' is not in the line (no ਭੀ here, unlike the refrain in a13.p2 and a13.p3).
fix: One who maligns a Sant is ever impure. One who maligns a Sant is no one's friend. One who maligns a Sant is punished. One who maligns a Sant is abandoned by all. One who maligns a Sant is utterly proud. One who maligns a Sant is ever given to vice. One who maligns a Sant is born and dies. Through slander of a Sant, one strays from peace. One who maligns a Sant has no place to stand. Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, he is brought into union.

problem: ਉਝੜਿ ਪਾਈਐ is to be put on the wrong road, off the path (our Hindi: कुमार्गपर डाल दिया जाता है); 'desolate places' only repeats the wilderness (ਉਦਿਆਨ) of the line before and loses the sense of straying.
fix: One who maligns a Sant breaks down halfway. One who maligns a Sant reaches the end of no task. One who maligns a Sant is made to wander in the wilderness. One who maligns a Sant is thrown off the path. One who maligns a Sant is hollow within, like the body of the dead without breath. One who maligns a Sant has no root at all; such people themselves eat what they themselves have sown. One who maligns a Sant has no one else to protect him. Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, even he is rescued.

problem: ਉਝੜਿ: English gloss has only 'into desolation'; the line needs the sense the Hindi already gives (कुमार्गपर): off the path, astray.
fix: ਉਝੜਿ: कुमार्गपर, उजाड़में | into desolation / off the path, astray

problem: Word order 'remember in Simran (meditative remembrance) the Lord, the King' is awkward; put the object first.
fix: Salok. Give up your cleverness, O good people, and remember the Lord, the King, in Simran (meditative remembrance). Keep in your mind the hope of the one Lord alone; Nanak, then pain, doubt and fear depart.

problem: Kirtan is glossed in apposition here ('Kirtan, the praise of God') but as 'Kirtan (sung praise)' in a15.p6 and a16.p8 and in the refrains file; use the one gloss.
fix: One who, by the Guru's grace, comes to understand his own self: know that his craving is quenched. One who speaks the praises of the Lord in the Saadh Sangat, that servant of the Lord stays free of all disease. One who night and day utters only Kirtan (sung praise), he alone is free of attachment while living as a householder. The person whose hope rests on the One alone has the noose of Death cut away. One who hungers in his mind for the Supreme Lord, Nanak, no sorrows cling to him.

problem: Agree with the writer's doubt: plural ਕਰਹਿ takes ਉਨ (the servants) of the line before as subject; our Hindi makes it God (वे (प्रभु)) and turns ਬਡਭਾਗੈ into a means (बड़े भाग्यसे).
fix: जिन्होंने प्रभुको जाना, वे शोभावाले हैं; उनके उपदेशसे सारा संसार उबर जाता है। प्रभुके सेवक सबका उद्धार करनेवाले हैं। प्रभुके सेवक दुःख भुला देनेवाले हैं। कृपालु (प्रभु) उन्हें स्वयं (अपनेसे) मिला लेता है; गुरुका शब्द जपकर वे निहाल हो जाते हैं। उनकी सेवामें वही बड़भागी लगता है, जिसपर वे (सेवक) कृपा करते हैं। नाम जपनेसे वे विश्राम पाते हैं। हे नानक! उन पुरुषोंको उत्तम मानो।

problem: Agree with the writer's doubt: ਓਇ (they, the servants) are the treasures of peace and ਉਨਹੂ ਬਨਿ ਆਏ is it befits them alone (glossary ਬਨਿ: फबकर); our Hindi makes God the treasure and has the servants become like him.
fix: (प्रभुका सेवक) जो कुछ करता है, प्रभुके प्रेममें करता है; वह सदा-सर्वदा हरिके संग बसता है। सहज स्वभावसे जो होता है, वह होता है; वह उस कर्तारको पहचानता है। प्रभुका किया हुआ सेवकको मीठा लगता है। (प्रभु) जैसा है, वैसा ही दिखायी देता है। जिससे वे उत्पन्न हुए, उसीमें समा गये। वे सुखके खजाने बन जाते हैं; यह (पद) उन्हींको फबता है। अपने-आपको (सेवकके रूपमें) उसने स्वयं मान दिया है। हे नानक! प्रभु और उसके सेवकको एक ही जानो।

problem: Agree with the writer's doubt: ਵਰਤੈ is intransitive (prevails, pervades) and ਪਾਸਾਰੁ is a noun (the expanse), so 'सच बरतता है, सच ही फैलाता है' misreads both; ਆਕਾਰੁ, ਪਾਸਾਰੁ are the visible world as the devotee sees it.
fix: जिसके मनमें गुरुपर विश्वास है, उस जनके चित्तमें हरि-प्रभु आ बसता है। तीनों लोकोंमें वह भक्त, भक्त कहकर सुना जाता है, जिसके हृदयमें एक (प्रभु) ही है। उसकी करनी सच्ची है, उसकी रहनी सच्ची है; उसके हृदयमें सच है, मुखसे वह सत्य कहता है। उसकी दृष्टि सच्ची है, (उसे) सारा आकार (दृश्य जगत्) सच्चा दिखता है; (सर्वत्र) सत्य (प्रभु) ही व्याप रहा है और सारा पसारा सच्चा है। जिसने पारब्रह्मको सच्चा करके जाना, हे नानक! वह जन सत्य (प्रभु) में समा गया।

problem: ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਪਰਮੇਸੁਰ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਾਨ ਦਇਆਲ ਬਖਸੰਦ are vocatives leading into ਸਾਧ ਤੇਰੇ (your Saadhs); rendered as a statement (He is ...), so the following 'your' has no one addressed and reads as a slip.
fix: Ashtapadi. Keep the Imperishable God in your mind. Give up your love for human beings. Beyond him there is nothing and no one; the One alone is present within all. He himself is all-seeing, he himself all-knowing; deep, profound, unfathomable and all-wise. O Supreme Lord, Transcendent Lord, Gobind, treasure of mercy, compassionate and forgiving One, may I fall at the feet of your Saadhs (holy ones): this is the longing in Nanak's mind.

problem: ਅਵਰ ਨ ਬੂਝਿ ਕਰਤ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ says no one else can understand and reflect on it; 'or gives thought to it' says no one else even thinks about it, which is not the point (our Hindi: चाहे विचार करे).
fix: True is the word, the teaching of the Saadh. True are the people in whose hearts it comes to dwell. If anyone comes to understand love for the True One, by chanting the Naam he attains salvation. He is true himself, and true is everything he has made. His own measure and state he alone knows. Whose creation it is, he is its maker. No one else can understand it and reflect on it. The Creator's limit is not known by what he has created. Nanak, whatever pleases him comes to pass.

problem: 'The attention is true' is unclear in English; ਸੁਰਤਿ here is the attentive hearing that receives his praise (our Hindi: सुरति (कान)).
fix: Ashtapadi. His feet are true, and those who touch them are true. His worship is true, and those who serve him are true. The sight of him is true, and those who behold it are true. His Naam (Name) is true, and those who meditate on it are true. He himself is true, and all that he upholds is true. He himself is virtue, and he himself bestows virtue. His Shabad (Word) is true, and the one who speaks of God is true. Attentive hearing is true, and the one who listens to his praise is true. To one who understands, all is true. Nanak, true, true is that God.

problem: 'he dwells there': 'there' has no antecedent (ਭੈ ਤੇ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਹੋਇ ਬਸਾਨਾ: freed from fear, he lives fearless).
fix: One who has believed in his heart in the Embodiment of Truth has recognised the Doer, the One who causes all to be done, as the root. One into whose heart faith in God has come, in his mind the essence of wisdom is revealed. Freed from fear, he lives without fear; he merges into the One from whom he sprang. When one thing is taken and blended into its own substance, it can no longer be called separate. One with understanding understands this discernment. Nanak, meeting the Lord, he becomes one with him.

problem: ਕਰਨ ਆਘਾਨੇ: the ears are sated, satisfied; 'filled' is ambiguous (filled with what?).
fix: Fruitful is the sight of him; beholding him, one becomes pure. Touching his feet, one's state and way of life become pure. Meeting him in his company, one dwells on the virtues of the Lord, and reaches the court of the Supreme Lord. Hearing his words, the ears are satisfied. Contentment comes into the mind, and the soul is at rest. Perfect is the Guru, everlasting his teaching. One upon whom he looks with his nectar glance becomes a Sant (saint). Endless are his virtues; his worth cannot be assessed. Nanak, whoever pleases him, him he unites with himself.

problem: Agree with the writer's doubt: ਦੇਇ has the same subject as ਲੇਇ before and ਰਾਖੈ after (the one in whose mind the treasure of virtues is revealed); our Hindi inserts (प्रभु).
fix: यह हरि-रस कोई विरला जन ही पाता है; जो यह अमृत पीता है, वह अमर हो जाता है। जिसके मनमें गुणोंका खजाना (प्रभु) प्रकट हो गया, उस पुरुषका कभी विनाश नहीं होता। वह आठों पहर हरिका नाम लेता है और अपने सेवकको सच्चा उपदेश देता है। उसे मायाके मोहका लेप नहीं लगता; वह मनमें एक हरिको ही रखता है। (मानो) घोर अँधेरेमें दीपकका प्रकाश हो गया। हे नानक! वहाँसे भ्रम, मोह और दुःख भाग जाते हैं।

problem: ਜਿਸ ਕਾ ਸਾ: ਸਾ is singular (was); 'whose own they were' makes it plural.
fix: In the burning heat, coolness has spread. Bliss has come, and the pains have fled, O brother. The anxieties of birth and death are gone through the perfect teachings of the Saadh (the holy one). Fear is ended, and they dwell fearless; all ailments are destroyed and have fled from the mind. The One to whom one belonged has shown grace. In the Saadh Sangat (the congregation of the holy), chant the Name of Murari, the Lord. Stability is found and the wandering of doubt is ended, Nanak, by hearing with the ears the praises of the Lord.
